### Interactive stories and games / 互动故事与游戏
- [Interactive stories and games](https://zenstory.ai/guides/interactive-games) — Turn a novel into player actions, branching stories, and a playable game.
- [Adapt a novel into a game: pick a playable slice, then build](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/quick-start) — Start with a novel you own or are authorized to adapt, then choose a bounded experience in which a player can act and see a consequence. A useful first slice keeps the source’s particular pressure while limiting scenes, systems and assets. Novel to Game’s seven skills take an agreed brief through analysis, concept and design to a built candidate. The ferry example below shows how to choose the scope before building; a playable result needs a built candidate that passes its runtime checks. Once a candidate exists, sort each comment into a misleading line, a result that breaks the approved rules or a new design request before asking for another build. The author-feedback examples below show how to keep the next change small and handle a different story as a new design decision.
- [Adapt a novel scene into meaningful choices and endings](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/meaningful-choices) — Start with what the player can change, and put choices only there. Make an important decision’s trade-off understandable, then write a response that preserves what the player actually chose. This original ferry scene goes from source facts to two decision points, advance information, a confirmation exchange and three different ending passages. A meaningful choice can also converge on an existing ending as long as its route history carries through, and expressive wording has a place too when it is presented as flavor. What follows is an editorial design draft, written before any build or playtest.
- [Choosing Gameplay for a Novel Adaptation: Start with Repeated Actions](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/choose-gameplay) — Use recurring actions, rules and costs to compare puzzles, management and interactive narrative. See three original designs and a fill-in concept card.
- [How to Design Resource Costs: Calculate Every Route to Its End](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/resource-cost-design) — Calculate energy, sampling, and return costs in a rover level, then fix accidental dead ends and dominant solutions while preserving clear choices.
- [How to Design a Game’s Core Loop](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/gameplay-core-loop) — Define player goals, actions, world rules, state changes, and readable feedback, then test the loop with a complete Paper City path.
- [How to Design a Game Level](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/game-level-pacing) — Plan level pacing with entry states, new decisions, visible responses, and end markers; recombine learned rules instead of adding enemies and puzzles.
- [How to Design Game Feedback Players Can Understand](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/readable-gameplay-feedback) — Design feedback around pre-action conditions, input responses, state changes, outcomes, and next steps, with an original mechanical post office example.
- [How to Design Game Failure and Restarts](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/game-failure-and-restart) — Distinguish hard failure, soft failure, and weaker outcomes. Define what is lost or preserved, where play resumes, and the state restored on restart.
- [How to Design an AI Text Adventure Without Invented Outcomes](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/llm-text-games) — Use a compact turn card to connect current facts, player action, conditions, actual change, and narration without inventing success.
- [Turn a Novel into an AI Text Adventure: Start with One Scene](https://zenstory.ai/dsh/deepseek-text-adventure) — Adapt one novel scene into an AI text adventure. Preserve source facts, define the player’s goal and choices, and test one path before expanding.
- [How to Organize AI-Assisted Voice Lines for a Small Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/game-voice-assets) — Track approved game lines by ID, speaker, trigger, subtitle, source, output, and fallback; check pronunciation, skip, mute, missing audio, and restart.
- [How to Design Multiple Endings That Reflect Player Choices](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-multiple-endings-in-a-game) — Tie endings to a small set of tracked decisions, make each outcome resolve the central promise, and show the cost of the chosen route.
- [How to Write a Visual Novel Script with Clear Routes](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/write-a-visual-novel-script) — Plan the common route, define what opens each character route, and write dialogue with clear speaker, scene, and choice state.
- [How to Write a Game Quest with a Clear Goal and Payoff](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/write-a-game-quest) — Give each quest a player-readable goal, a reason to act, meaningful steps, and a reward that changes future options.
- [How to Write Video-Game Dialogue That Fits Play](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/write-video-game-dialogue) — Keep lines tied to character goals and game state, avoid narrating visible actions, and test dialogue in the actual interaction.
- [How to Tell a Story Through a Game Environment](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/tell-a-game-story-through-the-environment) — Use object placement, damage, access, and repeated locations to show what happened and what players can infer.
- [How to Playtest a Novel-to-Game Adaptation](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/playtest-a-novel-game-adaptation) — Test whether players understand the game's goals, source identity, choices, and story feedback without relying on your explanation.
- [How to Plan a Branching Game Story](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/map-a-branching-game-story) — Choose a branch structure and preserve consequences at shared scenes. Includes an original investigation map, state variants and a practical content budget.
- [How to Design a Relationship System for a Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-a-relationship-system) — Define how trust and promises alter behavior before adding affinity scores. Includes concrete states, threshold checks and responses beyond repeated gifts.
- [How to Prototype a Narrative Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/prototype-a-story-driven-game-vertical-slice) — Test knowledge, choices and consequences in one complete scene before expansion. Includes an original scope, contrasting play paths and local failure diagnosis.
- [How to Design Randomness Around Player Decisions](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-game-randomness) — Define what randomness changes while preserving readable choices and consequences. Includes an original ferry game, dead-end checks and seeded comparisons.
- [How to Preserve Choices in Story-Game Saves](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-story-game-saves) — Separate current state from event history and preserve promises, knowledge and delayed consequences. Includes an original festival save table and reload checks.
- [How to Design NPCs With Goals and Memory](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-game-npcs) — Give NPCs desires, leverage, knowledge and active responses, with depth matched to their role. Includes an original vendor who does more than wait for clicks.
- [How to Design Clues for a Story Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-clues-for-a-detective-game-adaptation) — Separate evidence, supported conclusions and uncertain explanations. Includes an original ticket mystery with observation, questions and earned reveals.
- [How Much of a Novel Should a Game Adapt?](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/scope-a-novel-game-adaptation-for-a-small-team) — Separate source understanding from production scope. Preserve defining rules and tensions with an original adaptation table and a complete playable goal.
- [How to Simplify a Story Game Interface](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/organize-a-story-game-interface) — Separate persistent signals, current evidence and archives. Includes an original harbor scene and interface repairs that preserve readable text.
- [How to Fix a Game Screen That Is Too Dark](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/fix-an-overly-dark-game-interface) — Separate atmosphere from essential visual information. Includes an original night warehouse, four readability layers and viewport checks.
- [How to Define an Ancient-Fantasy Game Art Style](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/define-an-ancient-fantasy-game-art-style) — Calibrate period, visual medium and character treatment separately. Includes an original canal-city game, feedback repairs and an in-game target frame.
- [How to Design Skippable Game Cutscenes](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-skippable-game-cutscenes) — Make cutscenes read confirmed state and define boundaries and fallbacks. Includes an original lighthouse sequence and skip-path checks.
- [How to Write Clear Interactive Story Choices](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/write-clear-interactive-story-choices) — Make options state real actions, with distinct cost cues and responses. Includes an original testimony scene and boundaries for hidden consequences.
- [How to Design Deadlines in a Story Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-time-limits-in-a-story-game) — Define time advancement, commitments and visible deadline consequences. Includes an original ferry task and checks for early or repeated triggers.
- [How to Integrate AI Media into a Story Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/put-ai-media-assets-into-a-story-game) — Save generated media as stable game assets, connect it to state triggers and retain a fallback. Includes an original ferry scene and failure checks.
- [Buttons or Free Text: Choose a Story Game Input](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/choose-buttons-or-free-text-input) — Choose input from player actions. Compare buttons and free text in an original courier task, with finite intent, clear costs and readable outcomes.
- [How to Analyze Gameplay References](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/analyze-gameplay-references) — Analyze references by actions, loops, pressure and mastery. Use an original adaptation worksheet to state what to borrow, omit and test.
- [Balance Game Numbers by Comparing Strategies](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/balance-game-numbers-by-comparing-strategies) — Define what breaks a tradeoff, compare strategies from the same start, then change the situation. Includes repair costs and deadline calculations.
- [Too Many Game Stats? Keep Those That Affect Choices](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/reduce-unused-game-stats) — Audit generation, spending, rule checks and feedback. Separate strategic resources, story facts and history with a repair-commission example.
- [How to Stop Game Characters Knowing Secrets Too Early](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/stop-characters-knowing-secrets-too-early) — Separate facts, player knowledge, and character knowledge. Use a private-note example to check disclosure, inference, and merged branches.
- [How to Design a Second Playthrough for a Story Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-a-second-playthrough-for-a-story-game) — Choose replay for another route, new judgment, or a different strategy. Keep real tradeoffs and knowledge boundaries without compulsory randomness.
- [How to Design Items for a Story Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-items-for-a-story-game) — Make items affect available actions. Includes a complete borrowed-flashlight design, failed uses, ownership, and save-state checks.
- [How to Design Locked Options in a Story Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-locked-options-in-a-story-game) — Explain current requirements without exposing unknown routes. Includes a permission-and-key example, stale-state handling, and counterchecks.
- [How to Design a Game Opening Tutorial](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-a-game-opening-tutorial) — Teach one core action through visible information, a recoverable mistake, and feedback. Includes a complete opening delivery task and playtest questions.
- [How to Design Rewards in a Story Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-rewards-in-a-story-game) — Design rewards around later actions and check award, use, and callbacks. Includes two poster-stall upgrade paths beyond a larger number.
- [How to Design Exploration Routes in a Story Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-exploration-routes-in-a-story-game) — Connect readable landmarks, a main route, and optional routes to the current goal. Includes a sketchbook-return path with a remembered favor.
- [How to Fix a Story Game That Cannot Progress](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/fix-a-story-game-that-cannot-progress) — Check reachable actions from the current state, distinguishing unclear guidance, declared failure, and an unintended dead end. Includes a key-loan repair.
- [How to Connect Combat Results to a Game Story](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/connect-game-combat-results-to-the-story) — Make aftermath read actual results, choices, and delivered rewards. Includes two tournament paths without rewriting victory or making it solve every problem.
- [How to Design Puzzles for a Story Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-puzzles-for-a-story-game) — Fix the answer and rules, then connect visible clues to a real action. Includes a complete symbol-order puzzle, wrong answers, and an unread-clue route.
- [How to Design Crafting in a Story Game](https://zenstory.ai/novel-to-game/design-crafting-in-a-story-game) — Define crafting conditions, consumed materials, retained tools, and output ownership. Includes a complete prop-room route and failure cases.

### Video scripts and editing / 视频解说与剪辑
- [Video scripts and editing](https://zenstory.ai/guides/video-recaps) — Write narration from footage, edit a story, and finish audio and subtitles.
- [Export a video recap as an editable CapCut or JianYing draft](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/capcut-draft) — To keep editing a finished recap in JianYing or CapCut, export its existing timeline.json as an editable draft built from the source clips and per-segment narration. Video Recap Skills' standalone exporter puts the source clips with their original sound, the narration and optional music on separate tracks, keeps captions as text, and by default bundles the media into a draft folder under --out-dir, so the draft still opens after being moved. The export reads only the timeline and the media it references: ASR, visual understanding and TTS stay idle, and the rendered MP4 stays as it is. The rehearsal example below compares two edits, including what else has to move when a voiceover moves.
- [Make a video recap with Chinese narration from local footage](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/video-to-narration) — Video Recap Skills separates a Chinese-narration recap into understanding, editorial planning, narration, voiceover and assembly. Starting from an authorized local video, it builds a scene/speech/frame evidence index, chooses a viewer promise and POV, and writes only claims that evidence or supplied context supports. It can deliver a rendered MP4 or an editable draft. The source need not already have narration: the original no-dialogue example below compares two story angles and writes a short Chinese script that treats a promise written on screen as still untested. A separate partial-source variant covers footage that stops after the first attempts: request the missing payoff footage, or propose a narrower account and let the creator decide whether a fixed direction changes.
- [Video recap audio: keep the original sound or add narration?](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/original-audio-and-narration) — Let the sound that carries the event lead: a complete spoken line, a switch click or a meaningful wait tells its own part, so narration can stay out of its way. When viewers need context, say only what is supported and useful at that moment. This original radio example assigns five beats, then compares shortening a context sentence with removing it. Shortening keeps the owner’s reluctance to replace the radio without inventing poverty, and both options keep the wait after the switch fails to respond. Cutting narration leaves the dialogue captions in place; only extra commentary goes. The whole example stays at the written-plan stage; voiceover and mixing come later.
- [How to Write a Recap Script: Give Images and Narration Jobs](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/recap-script) — Build a recap around a promise to viewers, a main perspective and beats of change. Keep key original audio; narrate context, causality and interpretation.
- [Writing Clip Titles and On-Screen Text That the Video Supports](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/clip-titles) — Find a reason to watch that the clip can deliver. Give persistent titles, cover text, post titles, annotations and time-and-place labels distinct jobs.
- [How to Control Editing Rhythm: Cut Waiting, Keep Action and Reaction](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/editing-rhythm) — Judge rhythm through precise in and out points and reaction shots. Separate dead time from useful pauses with an original cut comparison and review method.
- [How to Edit Multiple Videos into One Complete Story](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/multi-video-story-edit) — Organize multiple videos around one question, story roles, changes, and evidence instead of file order. Includes an original three-source edit plan.
- [How to Research Before Writing a Video Recap](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/recap-background-research) — Research necessary relationships, prior events, and terms. Keep external context separate from current images and dialogue to avoid unsupported claims.
- [How to Lay Out Video Subtitles and Choose Line Breaks: Lock Picture and Sound, Then Check Sample Frames](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/subtitle-layout-and-line-breaks) — Separate spoken sentences from subtitle cues and line breaks, then inspect bright, dark, close-up, and long-caption frames for legibility and occlusion.
- [SRT Subtitles Out of Sync with AI Narration: Offset, Drift, or One Bad Cue?](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/subtitle-timing-evidence) — SRT early, late, or drifting from AI narration? Check the final video’s start, middle, and end, diagnose the pattern, repair it, and replay the render.
- [How to Write a YouTube Video Script Viewers Can Follow](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/write-a-youtube-video-script) — Define the viewer’s question, organize the answer into clear beats, and plan what the audience sees as well as hears.
- [How to Turn a Long Video into Short Clips That Stand Alone](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/turn-a-long-video-into-short-clips) — Choose moments with a complete point, add only the context needed to understand them, and make each clip’s title match its evidence.
- [How to Fix Flash Frames and Stray Shots in an Edit](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-flash-frames) — Distinguish stray frames from useful fast cuts, exposure changes and crop jumps. Inspect the rendered video, repair source boundaries and review the result.
- [How to Fix Music That Overpowers Speech](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/background-music-overpowers-voice) — Assign speech and music roles before adjusting levels. Includes an original recap audio table and checks against global volume changes and repeated mixing.
- [How to Keep Approved Audio When Changing Picture](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/keep-audio-when-changing-video) — Check whether picture changes alter timing, then pair independent picture and a complete soundtrack. Includes input checks, failures and subtitle rebinding.
- [How to Fix AI Voiceover That Runs Too Long](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fit-voiceover-to-a-picture-edit) — Compare authored text, spoken text, audio duration and output windows. Includes an original compression example and checks against clipping or excessive speed.
- [How to Keep AI Edit Revisions Local](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/revise-one-part-of-ai-edit) — Locate feedback by shot, sentence and time range, and record what this revision keeps. Includes a change list to prevent a small edit becoming a remake.
- [How to Dub an English Video into Chinese](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/translate-an-english-video-into-chinese) — Verify the English transcript and sentence translations before dubbing into the original windows. Includes an original demo and current workflow limits.
- [Fix Automatic Subtitle Errors in a Video Recap](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-automatic-subtitle-errors) — Correct names and negation against actual speech. Separate narration, dialogue and burned text, then choose the right subtitle source and clock.
- [How to Make a Video with Original Audio and No Voiceover](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/make-a-video-with-original-audio-and-no-voiceover) — Choose processed source audio, copying an adopted track, or pairing a new picture with a locked mix. Includes an operation request and listening checks.
- [How to Combine Landscape and Portrait Videos](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/combine-landscape-and-portrait-videos) — Choose a canvas for mixed video orientations, distinguish fitting from cropping, and check people, objects, subtitles, and cuts with a worked example.
- [How to Fix Dialogue Cut Off by a Video Edit](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-dialogue-cut-off-in-video) — Distinguish clipped speech, masking, and missing source audio. Restore complete source dialogue with an original borrowing example and updated output timing.
- [How to Fix Uneven Volume Between AI Voiceover Segments](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-uneven-ai-voiceover-volume) — Separate segment levels, peak guards, and final mixing. Includes gain examples and listening checks without confusing RMS targets with measured LUFS.
- [How to Fix Missing Words in AI Voiceover](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-missing-words-in-ai-voiceover) — Find whether words were shortened, omitted by TTS, or lost in assembly. Compare approved text, segment audio, and the current video.
- [How to Fix Long Pauses Between AI Voiceover Lines](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-long-pauses-in-ai-voiceover) — Separate silence inside a WAV, authored windows, pause settings, and actual placement. Includes a timing example that preserves intentional sound.
- [How to Fix a Video Export with No Sound](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-a-video-export-with-no-sound) — Check the current version, source streams, edited intermediate, voiceover segments, and final audio mode. A silence track cannot restore missing sound.
- [How to Fix Music Swells Between Voiceover Lines](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-music-swells-between-voiceover-lines) — Separate uneven voice segments from music repeatedly recovering in pauses. Includes a ducking-window example, short gaps, and intentional longer breaks.
- [How to Fix Inconsistent AI Voiceover Voices](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-inconsistent-ai-voiceover-voices) — Locate the audible change, then check requested voices, cached segments, and files used in the export. Includes a three-segment repair plan.
- [How to Improve Robotic AI Voiceover Delivery](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-robotic-ai-voiceover-delivery) — Check script flow, segmentation, supported delivery controls, and later speed changes. Includes a bounded example with exact text preserved.
- [How to Fix Repeated Lines in AI Voiceover](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-repeated-lines-in-ai-voiceover) — Separate repeated text, reused segment audio, and duplicate placement. Includes a repair plan that restores the intended second line.
- [How to Fix Pitch Changes After Speeding Audio](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-pitch-changes-after-speeding-audio) — Locate pitch changes in source audio, narration, or playback. Includes a ten-to-eight-second plan checking filters, cumulative speed, and listening.
- [How to Fix Video Audio Playing on One Side](https://zenstory.ai/video-recap/fix-video-audio-playing-on-one-side) — Separate playback faults, an empty channel, and intentional stereo. Includes a narration repair example and the limits of normalization and stream copy.


## Workbench docs
Product documentation for the ZenStory workbench only (the hosted browser app at https://app.zenstory.ai, project page https://zenstory.ai/workbench). Single URL per page, 中文 first with the English translation below. Index: https://zenstory.ai/docs — getting started, user guide, advanced, reference, troubleshooting.

- [Start writing in the browser workbench](https://zenstory.ai/docs/getting-started/quick-start): how to start in one session: create, target project files, request scoped help, save, export.
- [Write your first short story in ZenStory](https://zenstory.ai/docs/getting-started/first-project): a first short story from premise to TXT export, with facts, open choices and project files.
- [AI writing assistant: context and continuation](https://zenstory.ai/docs/user-guide/ai-assistant): how to give the assistant the right context: focused files, attachments, quotes, scoped requests and recovery.
- [Revise a passage in the workbench editor](https://zenstory.ai/docs/user-guide/editor): manual writing, quotations, review decisions, and save and conflict boundaries.
- [Use reference materials in the browser workbench](https://zenstory.ai/docs/user-guide/materials): TXT limits, asynchronous decomposition, result categories and explicit attachments.
- [Export a manuscript from the workbench](https://zenstory.ai/docs/user-guide/export): sequence-aware TXT export, a separate review copy, and bringing back offline edits.
- [Choose the scope of version recovery](https://zenstory.ai/docs/user-guide/version-history): file versions versus project snapshots, and comparing before recovery.
- [AI Memory: settings, progress and open ideas](https://zenstory.ai/docs/advanced/ai-memory): four editable project-summary fields, saved facts versus plans, and context budgets.
- [Browser writing workflow: decisions to saved prose](https://zenstory.ai/docs/advanced/workflow-tips): what to keep in context, what to save, and what the workbench does not promise.
- [Material analysis: source evidence to your own scene](https://zenstory.ai/docs/advanced/material-analysis): separate evidence from interpretation, then transfer the changed goal and cost into your own scene.
